summary: Re-review of the three hunks that landed since my pass at 443f267475b5, plus a re-verdict of the whole staged diff. All three deltas are checked against the code they name and hold up. (1) M4.8b1's return-vs-continue correction is TRUE: with the interposed `.delta.tmp` key mid-chain, `return` in place of `continue` at ChainReplay.applyChain truncates before the later deltas, leaving the GET count constant in the number of checkpoint keys seeded and no exception raised, so the prescribed offsets/nextSequence comparison against the same chain without the interposed key is what discriminates; CommitLog.nextOffset(RunKey) and nextSequence() are public, so the assertion is expressible. (2) `oldestRetainedOffset IS ZERO for every stream` is exact and cannot misfire against a correct writer -- there is no retention state anywhere in the tree and ChainReplay.fold produces only next offsets, so 0 is the only truthful value until M7 -- and it kills StreamOffsets(next, next); the retracted `the two fields differ` form was indeed both weaker (admits (next, next-1)) and sometimes false (a stream at offset 0). (3) Asserting the body's `sequence` against the key's does NOT conflict with the conditional same-key-for-a-T-tick criterion: a correct writer that rewrites the same key writes the same body sequence both times, so both criteria hold together. The baseline's third-and-fourth-mode clauses are true of the code: LocalSequencer.start calls predecessor.recoverChainEnd(), then seal(), then log.recover()/open(), and applyChain returns at the first Seal whose `%016x.delta` key sorts before `ckpt/`, so the takeover fixture that serves chainEnd genuinely destroys applyChain's. No object-store request-rate consequence: the change is specification prose and adds no get/put/list/stat; the row's cost paragraph and the AC5 zero-list bound are unchanged from the version I passed. Two minor findings, neither blocking under review.md `minors-land`.

findings.title: M4.8b2's new body-vs-key clause claims a coverage the conditional criterion does not have: the off-by-one derivation is reached by neither criterion, not just the constant-body one
findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog-notes.md, row M4.8b2 -- 'AND ASSERT THE BODY'S `sequence` AGAINST THE KEY'S ... it is the third of the three wrong `seq` derivations and the only one the conditional criterion above does not reach'
findings.detail: The row names three wrong `seq` derivations: (a) a per-checkpoint counter, (b) an off-by-one between last-included and nextSequence, (c) a constant body `Checkpoint.sequence` while keys increment. The conditional criterion -- strictly increasing across two triggers WITH DELTAS BETWEEN, and the SAME key for a T tick with no deltas between -- reaches (a): a counter increments on the no-delta tick and writes a different key, so it fails. It does NOT reach (b): both anchorings (key = last included sequence, key = nextSequence) increase strictly across triggers with deltas between AND produce the same key for a T tick with no deltas between. The new body-vs-key assertion does not reach (b) either, because an off-by-one applied consistently to key and body satisfies it. So (b) is reached by neither, and the clause's 'the only one the conditional criterion above does not reach' asserts otherwise. The only thing in the row that touches (b) is 'Decide which `seq` is and say so', which is an instruction to document, not a checkable criterion.
findings.suggested_remedy: One clause: say that the conditional criterion reaches only the counter, that the off-by-one is reached by neither it nor the body-vs-key assertion, and name the assertion that would -- the key's `seq` compared against the chain's own `nextSequence()` (or last committed sequence) at the moment of the trigger. Per review.md `minors-land` this can equally be recorded in the commit body or filed as a row; fixing it adds prose that becomes the next round's surface.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementer picks M4.8b2, reads the row, and concludes from this clause that the counter and the off-by-one are both covered by the conditional criterion and only the constant body needs a new assertion. They write body-vs-key, state in the row/javadoc that `seq` is the chain's nextSequence, and implement `seq` as the last-included sequence (or the reverse). Every prescribed assertion is green: keys are strictly increasing with deltas between, the same key repeats on a no-delta tick, the body matches the key, the grammar test pins padding. M4.9 is then built against the stated semantics and bounds replay from key+1 where the writer meant key: the delta at that sequence is never replayed, its offsets are lost, and a stream rewinds on the next recovery -- I2.

findings.title: The `oldestRetainedOffset IS ZERO` criterion kills the two named mutants only under a workload precondition the row does not state
findings.location: docs/internal/product/backlog-notes.md, row M4.8b2 -- 'the assertion that kills it is that `oldestRetainedOffset` IS ZERO for every stream' and the retraction clause naming `StreamOffsets(next, next - 1)'
findings.detail: The criterion cannot misfire against a correct writer -- that part is right, and it is a genuine improvement over 'the two fields differ'. But its discriminating power is conditional on the fixture: `StreamOffsets(next, next)` is caught only if some stream has nextOffset >= 1, and `StreamOffsets(next, next - 1)` -- which the clause explicitly claims as the reason the old form was worse -- is caught only if some stream has nextOffset >= 2 (at nextOffset 1 the mutant yields (1, 0) and the assertion passes; at nextOffset 0 it cannot even be constructed, since StreamOffsets refuses a negative oldestRetainedOffset). The row's nearest precondition is 'a workload where they differ', which is about per-stream and per-pod values differing from each other, not about any stream having committed at least two records.
findings.suggested_remedy: Add the precondition to the clause: assert it over a workload where at least one stream stands at nextOffset >= 2, which is the same workload the per-stream 'values differ' clause already wants.
findings.failure_scenario: The implementer reuses the first-post-takeover-checkpoint fixture (the one the row demands for the empty-pods hazard) for the decode-what-was-PUT assertions, and that fixture commits one record per stream, as a minimal takeover fixture naturally does. Every stream sits at nextOffset 1. `StreamOffsets(next, next - 1)` writes (1, 0) for every stream, the 'oldestRetainedOffset is zero' assertion passes, and a writer that derives the retained offset from the next offset ships untested -- becoming wrong the moment M7 retention gives the field a meaning.
